front.title: TLS 1.3 and Certificate Identity for the Session Initiation Protocol

abstract.t: The specifications that define the use of TLS with the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) predate TLS 1.3 and the current guidance for representing and verifying the identity of a service in a certificate. As a result, [RFC3261] states a mandatory cipher suite that a TLS 1.3 implementation cannot offer, and the certificate identity rules of [RFC5922] are no longer consistent with [RFC9525]. This document updates both, specifying a TLS version and cipher suite baseline for SIP and revising the representation and matching of SIP domain identities in certificates.
